title: Dissent to win
coreMove: Give the strongest objection a protected place before the group locks its choice.
sourcePressure: The chapter scales truth-seeking from one buddy to group culture, using dissent and CUDOS-style norms to keep consensus from impersonating evidence.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must make dissent procedural and evidence-seeking, not a personality trait of the bravest person in the room.

sourceAnchors.name: CUDOS
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source bundle lists CUDOS as the group-culture framework: communism, universalism, disinterestedness, and organized skepticism.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: CUDOS gives dissent a job description, so challenge belongs to the work instead of to the loudest personality.

sourceAnchors.name: organized skepticism
sourceAnchors.detail: The source describes organized skepticism as civil, active, structurally welcomed dissent.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Organized skepticism means the objection gets a chair before the decision leaves the room.

sourceAnchors.name: withheld uncomfortable facts
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source says an uncomfortable omitted fact often signals that the omitted fact matters most.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The fact everyone avoids may be the one carrying the most information.

tryThisNow: Invite dissent in your next meeting

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: aerospace parts safety review before supplier approval
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small tolerance concern could become a costly recall or safety incident
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas gives the dissenting tolerance note a formal slot on the approval agenda before the supplier vote can close.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A tray of machined brackets sits under a magnifying lamp at the end of the conference table.

exampleSpecs.domain: neighborhood flood committee choosing a levee design
exampleSpecs.stakes: polite consensus may hide that one street absorbs most of the overflow risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Whose street disappears from the map if everyone nods? Ingrid asks each design supporter to name the strongest objection before the vote.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Whose street disappears from the map if everyone nods?

exampleSpecs.domain: orchestra programming council selecting a risky season opener
exampleSpecs.stakes: a consensus favorite may be artistically exciting but financially fragile
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula assigns one council member to argue the ticket-risk case from subscription data, then makes the room answer it before applause decides.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Violin cases click shut outside the rehearsal hall while the program list waits on the piano.

exampleSpecs.domain: university ethics board reviewing a data-sharing proposal
exampleSpecs.stakes: source prestige could silence the junior member who sees a consent problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi shows how the ignored consent question should have been judged by the same standard as the senior researcher’s claim.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took the complaint letter to reveal which objection the board had treated as impolite.

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant opening crew deciding whether the kitchen is ready
exampleSpecs.stakes: opening on schedule could burn first reviews if the line cooks are not ready
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Anna move the objection from hallway whisper to prep-meeting agenda item, then require the team to test the weakest station before opening night.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can hear the ticket printer test from the empty dining room.

exampleSpecs.domain: cybersecurity incident table before a breach disclosure decision
exampleSpecs.stakes: withholding an uncomfortable log entry could delay notification and increase legal exposure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 1:27 a.m., Lukas asks why the log entry no one wants in the summary is not first on the evidence list.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 1:27 a.m., Lukas stares at the access log glowing blue on the war-room screen.

skillTargets: separate evidence conflict from ego conflict
use CUDOS norms in scenario choices
spot false confidence created by consensus

tryThisNowSpec: In the next group decision, write the strongest objection as a numbered agenda item before anyone votes, and require the room to answer it in evidence terms.
